summary: No strong R9 candidate found. The C++ hash tree (sparse, dense, page cache, dirty-page tree), the persisted hash-tree files (store, clone, rollback copy, clear_hash_tree rebuild), update_words and update_page, back_merkle_tree::pad_back, the collect_* computation-hash builders and the outputs and computation-tree constructions were reviewed. A differential experiment (live root hash vs a rebuild from a stored copy loaded with clear_hash_tree, plus verify_hash_tree) after run, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes (bundles 0 and 3), log_step_uarch x50, log_reset_uarch and collect_mcycle_root_hashes on the valid-template matched every time. Two weak candidates follow.

candidates.title: get_uarch_pristine_hash() and UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH return the Keccak-256 pristine uarch hash on a SHA-256 machine
candidates.component: machine API (C cm_get_uarch_pristine_hash, Lua machine:get_uarch_pristine_hash, JSON-RPC machine.get_uarch_pristine_hash); src/machine.cpp machine::get_uarch_pristine_hash; uarch/compute-uarch-pristine-hash.cpp
candidates.role: Honest operator only where a production node calls it on its path; the off-chain uarch replay (Support) uses the same constant. When unsure, both ratings are given below.
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp:2229-2233 (static, copies the uarch_pristine_hash[] array); src/cm.cpp:1112-1121 (takes a machine pointer but ignores its hash function); uarch/compute-uarch-pristine-hash.cpp main() (hard-codes hash_function_type::keccak256); also used by src/uarch-replay-state-access.hpp:369 and src/machine.cpp:2787
candidates.description: The pristine uarch state hash is precomputed only for Keccak-256. The per-machine method cm_get_uarch_pristine_hash(m) returns that constant even when m was created with hash_tree.hash_function = "sha256". It does not return the hash of the machine's own pristine uarch subtree. R9 requires precomputed hashes to be correct for every supported hash function, and SHA-256 is a supported hash-tree function. The uarch itself is refused on SHA-256 machines (reset_uarch, log_*_uarch and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes throw 'microarchitecture can only be used with hash tree configured with Keccak-256 hash function'), so no transition is affected. Only the value the API reports is wrong.
candidates.trigger: A trusted API caller creates or loads a SHA-256 machine and calls get_uarch_pristine_hash() on it, for example to compare it with get_node_hash(UARCH_STATE_START_ADDRESS, UARCH_STATE_LOG2_SIZE).
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any configuration with hash_tree.hash_function = "sha256". No guest action is involved.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? It needs a SHA-256 machine, which the manual reserves 'for use with the ZK prover' (doc/README.md, hash_tree entry), and 'ZK proving' is out of scope in AUDIT.md. If that exclusion covers every SHA-256 machine, the candidate is out of scope. 2 Role: the machine API. No referee verifier or PRT recipe calls it on a SHA-256 machine, so at most Honest operator where a node plausibly calls it, otherwise Support. 3 High/Medium cases: THREAT_MODEL section 8 Medium lists 'A hash-integrity defect that shows only under a hash function that no referee verifier supports (R9)'. The defect shows only under SHA-256, and no referee verifier supports SHA-256 (the uarch verifiers are Keccak-only), so this case applies. R9 says: 'Precomputed hashes, such as those of empty subtrees, must be correct for every supported hash function.' Rating: Medium if SHA-256 machines are in scope apart from ZK, otherwise Out of scope. 4 Critical: no, it is not on the honest operator's path of a Keccak deployment. 5 Low if triage reads the uarch constant as Keccak-only by design.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (or Out of scope as ZK-only; Low if the constant is Keccak-only by design)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not threaten the goal of section 1, because the uarch refuses SHA-256 machines. It still breaks the R9 obligation on precomputed hashes for every supported hash function: a per-machine query returns a hash that the machine's state does not commit to.
candidates.evidence: Ran scratchpad/campaign/r1/R9/exp2.lua on the baremetal-template config with hash_tree.hash_function="sha256". m:get_uarch_pristine_hash() returned 89ae34ba...43d7 (the Keccak constant), while m:get_node_hash(0x400000, 22) on the freshly created, pristine uarch returned 6da468a3...02f8. collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes was refused with the Keccak-only message.
candidates.test_idea: Create a SHA-256 machine from a minimal config. Assert that m:get_uarch_pristine_hash() equals m:get_node_hash(cartesi.UARCH_STATE_START_ADDRESS, cartesi.UARCH_STATE_LOG2_SIZE) right after creation, or that the call raises an error on non-Keccak machines. The test exits 1 today.

candidates.title: update_words writes parent hashes above a small range's dense-tree root into a process-global mutable 'no_hash' scratch
candidates.component: hash tree (src/hash-tree.cpp hash_tree::update_words; src/i-dense-hash-tree.hpp i_dense_hash_tree::no_hash_view; src/dense-hash-tree.hpp to_index)
candidates.role: Honest operator (hash tree; collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes uses update_words)
candidates.location: src/hash-tree.cpp:810-894 (max_level_count taken across all changed ranges; the loop at 878-894 hashes every curr_dense_node entry at every level up to max_level_count-1); src/i-dense-hash-tree.hpp:60-63 (returns a reference to a function-local static non-const machine_hash); src/dense-hash-tree.hpp:107-118 (an out-of-range level returns no_hash_view())
candidates.description: update_words climbs all dirty dense trees together for max_level_count-1 levels, where max_level_count is the largest level count among the ranges touched. For a smaller range (the one-page shadow uarch state, or the eight-page shadow state, next to uarch RAM or RAM), levels at and above its own root are out of range. There dense_hash_tree::node_hash_view returns i_dense_hash_tree::no_hash_view(), a function-local static non-const machine_hash shared by every dense tree of every machine in the process. update_words then writes concat(root, no_hash), and later concat(no_hash, no_hash), into that static. Two consequences follow. (a) Two machines in different threads of one process (for example a node that defends several epochs at once) that both run collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes race on the static. That is undefined behavior on the claim-building path. (b) The static also stands in for the 'empty' answer of empty_dense_hash_tree::root_hash_view(), so it no longer reads as zero after the first such call. By inspection, no in-range node is ever computed from the static, and no range registered in the hash tree uses empty_dense_hash_tree today. So no wrong root hash was found. The defect is latent.
candidates.trigger: The honest operator calls collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes. Every uarch cycle dirties words in the shadow uarch state (level count 1) and usually in uarch RAM or RAM (larger level counts) within one update_words call.
candidates.reachability: Reached on every uarch-level claim. The race needs two machines hashing concurrently in one process.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No exclusion applies. 2 Role: hash tree, Honest operator per the AUDIT.md table. 3 High/Medium cases: no listed case applies. No divergence or wrong hash was demonstrated, and the static's value never reaches an in-range node. 4 Critical? R1 forbids a canonical hash that depends on 'Thread count or parallel scheduling' or on 'Undefined behavior'. A data race on a shared static is UB in C++. But the racing writes only reach a value that no hash reads, so no canonical hash is shown to depend on it. Critical would need a demonstrated effect on a hash. 5 Low: a real defect (shared mutable scratch written out of range, a data race across machines) with no demonstrated rule violation.
candidates.threat_to_goal: There is no demonstrated threat today. The shared static is written out of range and races between machines in one process, so a future change that reads an out-of-range dense node or registers a range without a dense tree would silently fold arbitrary bytes into a state hash, against R9 and R1.
candidates.evidence: Code inspection only. dense_hash_tree::to_index returns invalid_index for level >= m_level_count, and the mutable overload of do_node_hash_view then returns no_hash_view(), which is static, shared and writable. The update_words loop at hash-tree.cpp:878 is bounded by max_level_count across ranges, not by each range's own level count. update_dense_trees has a per-range guard ('if (level > ar.get_level_count()) continue;'), which update_words lacks.
candidates.test_idea: A C++ unit test (or a debug assertion) that runs update_words with dirty words in the shadow uarch state and in uarch RAM, then asserts that i_dense_hash_tree::no_hash_view() still reads all zeros. A ThreadSanitizer run of two machines doing collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes concurrently would report the race. The required behavior: update_words never writes outside a range's dense tree (skip a range once level >= its level count).

not_covered: machine-solidity-step generated code: did not check that its Merkle and proof handling (sibling order, heights, the pristine constants of UArchReset and SendCmioResponse) matches the emulator tree; only noted that UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH matches per the harness README
Dave contracts beyond reading Tree.sol and Commitment.sol (position range checks, match bisection heights and leaf/inner handling inside Match.sol and Tournament.sol were not traced)

cartesi-rollups-contracts output validation (CanonicalMachine and its outputs-tree constants for empty subtrees) and libcmt's outputs Merkle tree in machine-guest-tools: not compared with the Lua frontier helpers

Lua frontier_forest_* (store, load, merge_node, expand_leaf, descend_tree on fixed-point trees) and frontier_next_proofs: reviewed by reading only, no randomized differential test against a naive tree
prt.lua mcycle and uarch claim builders with bundling and fixed-point padding across restarts (player restart persistence of forests)
Hash-tree behavior under host faults or failures injected inside update() (for example page-cache exhaustion or a failed enqueue): reasoned about but not exercised
Shared (sharing_mode::all) machines: the phtc initialized-tag protocol and the dht/dpt files across destroy and sync were not exercised; no crash or restart experiments
replace_memory_range with a replacement that supplies its own dht/dpt files; jsonrpc fork/clone paths; the record-step (main-processor step log) proofs, which are ZK-only

SIMD hasher lane implementations (simd-hasher.hpp, the keccak and sha256 lane code) and the hash-tree-hash helper tool were not checked for correctness against scalar hashing beyond the end-to-end experiment

A large random-operation fuzz of the hash tree (write_memory, fill_memory, write_reg, TLB writes via the API, store/load/clone, clear_hash_tree) against full rehash: only one scripted differential sequence was run
